The cache's performance would affect both request migration and latency. If the cache is underutilized, more data needs to be sent to the workers, increasing tail latency.

Tail latency is the time it takes for a request to be processed once the tail is behind the current processing. If there are many workers, the tail latency could be reduced. But if there are too many workers, it might become a bottleneck.

Request migration. This is when a request moves from one worker to another. The system needs to decide which worker to assign to which request. If the prefill and decode workers are distributed, this could be managed through scheduling or some form of queueing. The migration time affects throughput and resource utilization.

Role switching. When a worker is assigned a task, it might switch roles. For example, a prefill worker could switch to decode. This affects GPU utilization and throughput. If the role switching is efficient, it can handle more requests without losing performance.

GPU utilization. Each worker has a GPU. If the system uses a hybrid model with GPU and CPU, the GPU's utilization can vary. The trade-off here is between using more GPU resources for higher throughput and managing the load without overutilizing the GPU.

Throughput tradeoffs. Throughput is the amount of data processed per unit time. If you increase the number of workers, throughput might go up, but each worker has a limited GPU and processing power. So there's a balance between the number of workers and how efficiently they use the resources.
